text: The rains fell in generous sheets, and the earth rewarded their shared toil.
By October, the groundnuts were dug, the yellow maize was husked, and the pearl millet stood stacked in golden sheaves.
Together, they built a tall, woven benteng raised on smooth wooden stilts, packing it to the roof with food to last through the lean months.
'No one shall touch a single grain,' Lion decreed in his rumbling voice, 'until the harmattan winds arrive and the village council approves.'
They locked the wooden door with a sturdy pad of baobab bark and went home to sleep.
